description: Declared mutants of the kernel spike (v8-arch-kernel-spike; docs/architecture/plans/kernel/spike-report.zh-Hant.md). A mutant is killed only when its check fails with the expected message: a build failure for the compile-time checks (expect_build_failure; each regex names the requirement this mutant must trip, checked against the AppleClang output), a failing doctest case otherwise. "note" is for readers; the runner ignores it. Configure the spike first (spikes/kernel/CMakeLists.txt), then run docs/architecture/plans/time-threads-trace/scripts/run_mutations.py --build-dir <spike build dir> --catalog spikes/kernel/mutations.json.

mutants.what: the page-guard fault handler lifts the protection but records nothing
mutants.expect: PageGuard Bypass \(L1\)
mutants.note: v8-arch-kernel-spike-pageguard. L1 is the shape only the page guard sees (no net change at the System boundary), so with nothing recorded its Run returns Ok.

mutants.what: a (b) System is guarded like a (c) System (only its declared writes lifted)
mutants.expect: PageGuard Control: a \(b\) System writes any column

mutants.what: Shared columns are page-guarded too (not only Exclusive ones)
mutants.expect: PageGuard Control: a Shared column is not guarded

mutants.what: the fault handler records the fault but does not lift the column's protection
mutants.expect: repeated fault on a guarded column whose protection was already lifted
mutants.note: v8-arch-kernel-spike-pageguard. Killed by a non-zero exit, as the batch declaration allows for this mutant: the write faults again on the same column, the handler finds it already recorded and aborts (SIGABRT) with the expected message instead of retrying forever. run_mutations.py already counts any non-zero exit whose output matches as a failure, so the runner is unchanged.

mutants.what: with pageGuard off the World still walks the guarded columns and asks for protection changes
mutants.expect: PageGuard Control: pageGuard off makes no protection call
mutants.note: v8-arch-kernel-spike-pageguard. No storage is page-guarded when the option is off, so the extra calls change no protection; the per-World call count is what shows them.

mutants.what: after a (c) System returns, the columns it declared as written stay writable for the rest of the Run
mutants.expect: PageGuard Bypass after Write<T>

mutants.what: after a (c) System returns, the columns the fault handler lifted are not protected again
mutants.expect: PageGuard Continue: a write to another World's guarded column
mutants.note: v8-arch-kernel-spike-pageguard r2 (adversary S3). Observable only through another World: a Run ends at its first Err and the next Run protects every column of its own World again on entry, so a lifted column of the Run's own World is never seen unprotected; another World's column stays lifted unless ProtectFaulted protects it again.
